sentenceSets.sentence: The media conglomerate owned dozens of outlets spanning print, broadcast, and digital platforms.

answerChoices.reasoning: A corporation is a single legal company pursuing one line of business, which fails to capture the sentence's picture of dozens of separate outlets in three different media held under one owner.
A syndicate is an alliance of separate parties pooling effort on a venture, whereas the sentence describes one entity that owns the outlets outright.
A monopoly requires that competitors be shut out of a market, but the sentence only counts what this owner holds and says nothing about rivals.
Empire is a loose metaphor for reach and influence, while the sentence is precise about a formal ownership structure covering named categories of outlet.
A network is a single broadcast system, too narrow for holdings that include print and digital as well.
A publisher works in print, which covers only one of the three platforms the sentence lists.
An agency acts on behalf of clients rather than owning dozens of outlets itself.
A partnership is a form of ownership among individuals, which says nothing about the sprawl across print, broadcast, and digital.
A cooperative is owned by its members, contradicting a single owner holding dozens of outlets.
A startup is young and small, incompatible with dozens of outlets across three platforms.
A charity does not own commercial media properties for profit.

sentenceSets.sentence: What began as a single shoe factory had become, after forty years of acquisitions, a conglomerate with holdings in insurance, shipping, and frozen food.

answerChoices.reasoning: A trust unites competing firms in one industry to control its market, but the holdings listed here are in three unrelated businesses.
A cartel is an agreement among independent rivals to fix terms, whereas the sentence describes one company absorbing others through acquisitions.
A chain repeats the same kind of outlet in many places, which cannot describe insurance sitting alongside shipping and frozen food.
A consortium is a temporary alliance of separate members for one project, but the sentence traces a single firm's growth over forty years of buying companies.
A manufacturer makes goods, which describes only the original shoe factory rather than what the company grew into.
A brand is a name and identity, not the structure that owns businesses in three unrelated sectors.
A subsidiary is owned by another company, reversing the direction of ownership the acquisitions established.
Enterprise is a generic word for any business venture and captures nothing about holdings spread across unrelated industries.
A boutique is small and specialized, contradicting forty years of acquisitions across three sectors.
A nonprofit does not build holdings in insurance and shipping through acquisitions.
A guild is an association of craftspeople, not an owner of frozen food businesses.

sentenceSets.sentence: Ash, sand, and shattered shell had fused over centuries into a conglomerate that geologists could date to the eruption.

answerChoices.reasoning: Aggregate names loose material gathered together, but the sentence stresses that these components fused into a single datable body of rock.
Composite is a general term for anything made of mixed materials, which would not tell a geologist that what is being dated is a rock formed in place.
An amalgam properly describes a metal alloy with mercury, and its figurative use covers blended ideas rather than a datable stratum of ash, sand, and shell.
Sediment is unconsolidated material that has settled out, whereas the sentence says the components fused over centuries into something solid.
A mineral is a single chemically uniform substance, contradicting a body made of three distinct materials.
Crust names the earth's outer layer as a whole, far larger than the local deposit the geologists dated.
Residue is leftover matter, which does not convey the fusing into rock that the sentence describes.
A matrix is the fine material surrounding embedded fragments, a part of such a rock rather than the rock itself.
A crystal has a regular internal structure, incompatible with shattered shell mixed into ash and sand.
A liquid could not be dated as a fused deposit centuries old.
Vapor is gaseous and cannot contain fused sand and shell.
